a1-unit-31.31.1 Doctor:
Host: Good morning and welcome back to Healthy Life! Today our doctor from São Paulo is here to answer your questions about fruit and vegetables. Good morning!
Ana: Good morning! I'm happy to be here.
Host: Our first question is from Bruno in Recife. How many servings of fruit and vegetables do I need every day?
Ana: The World Health Organization says at least five servings a day. And try to eat the rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green and purple food. Different colors give you different vitamins.
Host: Carla from Curitiba loves strawberries. She asks: How many strawberries are one serving?
Ana: Seven strawberries are one serving. With bigger fruit, it's easy. One banana or one apple is one serving.
Host: Pedro from Belo Horizonte doesn't eat many vegetables. He asks: How much corn is one serving?
Ana: Three big spoons of corn or peas are one serving. You can have them with your rice and beans.
Host: Next, Paula from Salvador. I don't really like vegetables. Can I eat only fruit?
Ana: Fruit is great, but you need vegetables too. Start with a little. Try a few carrots or a little broccoli at lunch.
Host: And our last question. Is juice healthy?
Ana: A small glass of juice is one serving, but only one. Two glasses of juice still count as one serving, and juice has a lot of sugar. So don't drink too much juice. Eat the fruit!
Host: Great advice. Thank you so much, doctor!
